title: Lute compiled IR artifact (irVersion 0.16.x)
description:
JSON Schema (draft 2020-12) for the WHOLE compiled Lute IR artifact emitted by `lute compile` (crates/lute-compile, ir.rs `Artifact`). One artifact is produced per `.lute` document; a project's engine unions the per-document `relations`/`rules`/`seedFacts`/`entities`/`enums`/`prereqEdges` across every artifact exactly as it unions the command streams.

VERSION-NEGOTIATION POLICY (spec §4.1, A9; relaxed in 0.13.0): an engine gates on `irVersion` by MAJOR only — it MUST accept any artifact whose `irVersion` MAJOR it implements and MUST refuse one from a different MAJOR. Minor and patch are compatible-by-default (fields are append-only within a major line; unknown fields are ignored), and an unknown command `kind` is the hard error that catches a genuinely newer capability. Pre-1.0, a breaking change may still land in a minor (0.10.0's provenance rename); such changes are called out in the CHANGELOG and this schema rather than fenced by the gate. `lute` (the language version) is informational for the runtime and does not gate parsing. Forward compatibility: an engine MUST IGNORE unknown OBJECT FIELDS (new optional fields are added append-only within a minor line) so a newer PATCH artifact still loads on an older engine of the same major.minor; an engine MUST treat an unknown command `kind` as an ERROR (a new command kind is a real capability the engine cannot fake). Field declaration order in an artifact is a byte-stability contract of the compiler but carries no semantics for a consumer.

IR 0.8.0: within one artifact every `addr` shares a field width, so lexicographic order over `addr` equals execution order (dsl 0.8.0 §2). Engines loading artifacts from mixed toolchain versions SHOULD still compare `addr` segment-wise numerically.

IR 0.9.0: a PURE RESTAMP of 0.8.0 for release-wide version alignment (docs/versioning.md) — lute-ir-0.9.schema.json IS lute-ir-0.8.schema.json renamed, with no field added, renamed, moved, or retyped.

IR 0.10.0: a REAL shape change, not a restamp (#36, dsl 0.10.0 Appendix B). `provenance.reason` is renamed to `provenance.explanation`; no command `kind` is added, renamed, or removed, and no other field changes. Because the gate above is by MAJOR.MINOR, an engine implementing IR 0.9 MUST refuse a 0.10.0 artifact; widening that gate and reading `provenance.explanation` are the only changes such an engine needs. lute-ir-0.9.schema.json is kept published for engines still on 0.9.

IR 0.11.0: a PURE RESTAMP of 0.10.2 for release-wide version alignment (docs/versioning.md) — lute-ir-0.13.schema.json IS lute-ir-0.10.schema.json renamed, with no field added, renamed, moved, or retyped. Unlike 0.10.1/0.10.2, which shared major.minor 0.10 and needed no rename, this release moves the gated major.minor itself (0.10 → 0.11), so the file renames and an engine implementing IR 0.10 MUST widen its gate before it accepts a 0.11.0 artifact — reading no new field, because there is none. lute-ir-0.10.schema.json is kept published for engines still on 0.10.

IR 0.15.0 reshapes sceneMeta (dsl 0.15.0 §2/§3, authored scene identity): sceneMeta gains the always-present `id` field (the resolved canonical scene key — authored `id:` verbatim, else the derived `{character}.{episodeId}` join); the four legacy identity keys (`character`/`season`/`episode`/`episodeId`) demote to optional; and BOTH sceneMeta and questMeta gain the descriptive `meta` block (an open mapping whose values are scalars or flat scalar arrays, key-sorted by the compiler, omitted when empty). The gated major.minor moves (0.14 → 0.15); lute-ir-0.14.schema.json is kept published for engines still on 0.14.

IR 0.16.0 is ADDITIVE-ONLY over 0.15.1 (dsl 0.16.0 declarative rewards): cmdQuest and objectiveEntry each gain an optional `rewards` array of the new `rewardEntry` def. Both arrays are omitted when empty, so a pre-rewards artifact stays byte-identical to 0.15.1. A `rewardEntry` carries `kind`, optional `target`, exactly one of `amount` XOR (`amountMin` + `amountMax`) after amount defaulting (unauthored → `amount: 1`), an optional `when` CEL pair evaluated at the grant instant, and `on: "failed"` on a quest-level entry (objective-level entries never carry `on`). Range amounts are wire-verbatim — an engine never sees a pre-rolled scalar (spec D-C). The runtime contract emits deterministic `grant` transcript events at each fresh lifecycle transition (spec §3 D-D); the reference engine's shape is `{ "kind": "grant", "quest": <id>, "objective": <oid>?, "reward": { …rewardEntry sans when… }, "onFailed": true? }`. The per-release rename rule renames `lute-ir-0.15.schema.json` → `lute-ir-0.16.schema.json`; the gated MAJOR does not move under 0.13.0's MAJOR-only runtime contract, so a 0.15 engine parses a 0.16.0 artifact unchanged and simply does not ask for the added arrays.

kind.description: document kind discriminator (dsl 0.2.0 §2/§3.1); read first — it selects `meta`'s shape.

lute.description: language-version pin (informational for the runtime), e.g. "0.7.0".

irVersion.description: IR schema version the engine gates on (MAJOR only since 0.13.0), e.g. "0.14.0".

capabilityVersion.description: plugin-system §13 capability snapshot stamp (a content hash); a consumer may refuse a mismatched snapshot.

state.description: the folded init/type table (§4.1); may be empty but is always present.

entities.description: merged relational entity kinds; omitted entirely when empty.

enums.description: merged relational enums; omitted when empty.

relations.description: merged relation declarations; omitted when empty.

seedFacts.description: merged seed facts (vocabulary order); omitted when empty.

rules.description: merged Datalog rules as DATA (vocabulary order); omitted when empty. Lute runs no fixpoint (D1).

prereqEdges.description: advisory raw `after` prerequisite edges (connectivity T13); omitted when empty.

shots.description: dsl 0.8.0 §6: authored `## ` shot headings, in document order. Omitted when no shot carries a heading. Quest documents have no shots.

injected.description: always `true`. Retained for IR compatibility; the compiler constructs no `false`, and a consumer MUST NOT read a `true` as distinguishing anything.

by.description: the named injection rule responsible, e.g. "auto-anchor-on-show".

explanation.description: human-readable justification, authored by the COMPILER in English for a human reader. Renamed from `reason` in IR 0.10.0 (#36): `end.reason` on the `end` command is an opaque author-written token a host dispatches on, and the two share no contract — `explanation` cannot be read as a dispatch key.

provenance.description: §4.3 injection provenance (lute_check::inject::Provenance): why an implicit command exists.

source.description: §4.3 component source stamp on component-expanded records (D8).

exprNode.description: Portable CEL expression AST (IR A7, expr.rs). Serialized as an UNTAGGED serde enum — each variant is a bare object distinguished by its keys. A plain JSON walker evaluates it; the parallel `raw`/string field carries the source CEL for debug. Absent whenever the CEL slot was empty or fell outside the closed Lute-CEL profile (dsl §8.4).

lit.description: scalar literal; every numeric CEL literal collapses to a double.

celPair.description: A CEL slot's raw text plus its optional portable lowered `expr` (IR A7). `expr` is absent for empty/out-of-profile CEL.

placeholder.description: One {{…}} interpolation placeholder (IR A3), internally tagged on `kind` (lowercase). The runtime substitutes it against live state; the enclosing text/label keeps the verbatim {{…}} marker.

role.description: :line role (§4.4). Voiced roles (dialogue/voiceover/offscreen) carry a voiceKey; monologue/narration do not.

members.description: closed member set; ABSENT for `open: engine` kinds (the engine mints members).

tier.description: effective write tier for base relations (default `run`); ABSENT for `derive: true` (a derived relation has no write tier).

key.description: 0-based functional-key arg indices (§4); absent when undeclared.

args.description: ground literals as strings; bools as "true"/"false". Never "_".

termEntry.description: One rule term (dsl 0.3.0 §7.1), tagged on `kind`. Bools lower to a Const with value "true"/"false".

atomEntry.description: One rule atom: a relation applied to terms (dsl 0.3.0 §7.1).

bodyEntry.description: One rule body literal (dsl 0.3.0 §7.1), tagged on `kind`: a positive/negated atom, a CEL guard, or a term comparison.

raw.description: the rule's original source text, for engine diagnostics.

ruleEntry.description: One Datalog rule (dsl 0.3.0 §7.1), emitted as STRUCTURED data. Lute performs NO evaluation (D1); the engine runs the least-fixpoint over this rule set.

node.description: the contributing node's canonical key: a scene's {character}.{episodeId} or a quest's <quest id>.

after.description: the RAW declared `after` formula text — unresolved, unvalidated CEL.

prereqEdgeEntry.description: One advisory prerequisite edge (connectivity spec §2.6, T13): a single node's raw declared `after`, verbatim.

id.description: dsl 0.15.0 §2: the resolved canonical scene key — authored `id:` verbatim, else the derived `{character}.{episodeId}` join. Always present on a scene artifact. Character set: [A-Za-z0-9_.-]+, non-empty. This is the identity every consumer (lineId prefix, prereqEdges[].node, project.index.json document key, connectivity visited() targets) joins on.

character.description: dsl 0.15.0 §2: OPTIONAL. On a document that authors `id:`, only the legacy identity keys the author WROTE survive into the artifact (a project-level defaults: fallback SHOULD NOT resurrect a dropped key). On the derived-key path (no `id:` authored), this field is present and resolved as in 0.14.0.

episodeId.description: See sceneMeta.character — OPTIONAL under dsl 0.15.0 §2. On the derived-key path this is the resolved value (authored episodeId verbatim, else `s{season:02}ep{episode:02}`), exactly as in 0.14.0.

extra.description: dsl 0.15.0 §3: free descriptive open mapping the checker admitted past E-META-VALUE. Values are scalars (string / integer / number / boolean) or FLAT sequences of scalars. Never consulted by any checker/compiler/runtime rule and never routed through CEL — the sanctioned home for team search metadata (`arc`, `location`, `tags`, whatever). Key-sorted by the compiler; absent when the document authors no `extra:` block.

plugin.description: plugin-system 0.0.4 §2: checker-validated, plugin-owned top-level frontmatter keys, key -> JSON value (any shape the declaring plugin's frontmatter schema admits, plugin-system 0.0.1 §6.8). Absent when the document authors no plugin-owned key.

sceneMeta.description: Scene-kind envelope meta (dsl 0.15.0 §2/§3). Present when `kind` == "scene". Since 0.15.0 only `id` is required — the four legacy identity keys demote to optional.

extra.description: dsl 0.15.0 §3: same descriptive block as sceneMeta.extra, sanctioned on quest roots too. Same scalar / flat-scalar-array shape; key-sorted; absent when the document authors no `extra:` block.

plugin.description: plugin-system 0.0.4 §2: checker-validated, plugin-owned top-level frontmatter keys, key -> JSON value. Absent when the document authors no plugin-owned key.

questMeta.description: Quest-kind envelope meta (dsl 0.2.0 §6.1, dsl 0.15.0 §3). MAY serialize as {} when none of title/contentLang/meta/plugin are authored. Present when `kind` == "quest".

domain.description: enum member domain; an implicit branch/quest-state slot appends "unset".

default.description: initial value (any JSON scalar/array/object), integral-collapsed. Absent when the slot has no default (maybe-unset).

provenance.description: "branch:<id>" for an implicit choice slot, "quest:<id>" for a reserved quest slot; absent for an author-declared slot.

stateEntry.description: One folded state slot (§4.1): the engine's init/type table entry.

effectSource.description: The origin of an Effect's value (IR A12, untagged).

bridgeResult.description: read the named key off the bridge call's returned result object.

anyOf.description: a bare literal value (manifest scalar), integral-collapsed.

path.description: fully-resolved dotted state path (scope + segments, fromAttr already substituted at compile time).

effect.description: A resolved plugin state-write binding (IR A12): where a bridge result / increment / literal lands. The runtime applies it after the bridge call — no manifest lookup, no per-plugin knowledge.

when.description: raw guard CEL; present only when the option is guarded.

labels.description: dsl 0.8.0 §7: merged locale labels, locale tag → text, keyed on `lineId`. Absent when no locale bundle was merged. The source-language string stays in `text`/`label`.

exit.description: leaves the hub loop when taken.

labels.description: dsl 0.8.0 §7: merged locale labels, locale tag → text, keyed on `lineId`. Absent when no locale bundle was merged. The source-language string stays in `text`/`label`.

hubOption.description: One <hub> option: a choice option plus always-present once/exit revisit flags.

test.description: raw arm guard CEL (debug); the executable form is `expr`.

kind.description: The reward kind id (dsl 0.16.0 §2). When a plugin publishes a `rewardKinds:` vocabulary (§4), the checker's `E-REWARD-KIND` closure gates this against the merged vocabulary; without a vocabulary, any non-empty string is accepted (shape-only mode).

target.description: Optional target id — the address of the effect target (e.g. an inventory owner). Its id-space is pinned by the reward-kind's `target: { provider: <name> }` declaration when the vocabulary declares one; a shape-only kind admits any target string.

amount.description: Scalar amount (dsl 0.16.0 §2, integers, negatives legal). Present when the authored `amount` was a scalar, or when the attribute was unauthored (defaults to `1` per Global Constraints amount defaulting). Mutually exclusive with `amountMin`/`amountMax`.

amountMin.description: Lower bound of a range amount (dsl 0.16.0 §2, `N..M`, `N <= M`). Carried verbatim from the authored value — a reference engine NEVER pre-rolls a value into `amount` (spec D-C); the engine's own dice draw over `[amountMin, amountMax]` at grant time is engine policy the IR does not fix. Present iff `amountMax` is present; both are mutually exclusive with `amount`.

amountMax.description: Upper bound of a range amount — see `amountMin` for the range contract.

when.description: Optional CEL gate evaluated at the grant instant (spec §3). Grants fire iff `when` decides Bool(true); a `false`/`unknown` gate silently skips the entry once (a transition is monotone and fires at most once, so `when` is a one-shot filter, not a re-triable predicate).

on.description: Optional lifecycle-transition filter (dsl 0.16.0 §2). Only ever `"failed"` on the wire, and only on a quest-level entry — a quest reward with `on="failed"` grants ONLY on a fresh `failed` transition (authored `fail` OR §2.3 cascade); absent `on=` means the reward grants ONLY on a fresh `complete`. Objective-level entries never carry `on=` (checker `E-REWARD-ATTR`).

rewardEntry.description: One `<reward kind= target= amount= when= on=/>` declaration (dsl 0.16.0 §2/§3). Pure data — the compiler NEVER synthesizes handler bodies or `Command::Set` records for a reward; the reference engine (`crates/lute-cli/src/runner.rs` `Runner::emit_grants`) emits deterministic `grant` transcript events at each fresh lifecycle transition, and `lute trace` mirrors those events (`crates/lute-trace/src/walk.rs`).

body.description: addr of the objective's completion-body segment; ALWAYS present, `null` when the body is empty.

quest.description: Referenced child quest id of a subquest objective (<objective quest=...>, language 0.14.0); the objective's done is the synthesized quest.<child>.state == 'complete'. Omitted for authored-done objectives.

rewards.description: dsl 0.16.0 §2/§3 declarative rewards — direct-child `<reward/>` entries of this objective in declaration order. Objective grants fire once at fresh `done` (spec §3 D-D), BEFORE any quest-level grant. `on=` is never legal on an objective-level entry (checker `E-REWARD-ATTR`); every entry here has no `on` field. Omitted when the objective authors no rewards (byte-identical to 0.15.1 for pre-rewards artifacts).

objectiveEntry.description: One objective inlined in QuestCmd.objectives (dsl 0.2.0 §6.4). Declaration data only; the engine derives completion (all non-optional objectives done ⇒ quest complete).

addr.description: the record's resolved address (§4.2), unique within the artifact; jump/converge/target/body fields point at these.

texts.description: dsl 0.8.0 §7: merged locale texts, locale tag → text, keyed on `lineId`. Absent when no locale bundle was merged. The source-language string stays in `text`/`label`.

costume.description: A1 schema-only: resolved costume id; never emitted until the cast plugin ships.

cmdSprite.description: An authored ::auto or an injected sprite command (§7.4); injected records carry `provenance` in the stamp.

value.description: raw RHS text; the executable form is `expr`.

addr.description: the record's resolved address (§4.2), unique within the artifact; jump/converge/target/body fields point at these.

cmdAssert.description: One asserted fact delta (dsl 0.3.0 §5). DATA only — the engine applies it as a positive write to the relation's fact set.

addr.description: the record's resolved address (§4.2), unique within the artifact; jump/converge/target/body fields point at these.

cmdRetract.description: One retracted fact delta (dsl 0.3.0 §5). The engine applies it as a negative write; "_" positions are a bulk wildcard the engine resolves.

addr.description: the record's resolved address (§4.2), unique within the artifact; jump/converge/target/body fields point at these.

prompt.description: dsl 0.11.0: the choice-situation sentence shown by the UI. Present only when authored.

timeoutSec.description: dsl 0.11.0: the countdown, in whole seconds, before the branch times out. Present only when authored.

addr.description: the record's resolved address (§4.2), unique within the artifact; jump/converge/target/body fields point at these.

cmdHub.description: <hub> (§7.3.2): a choice plus revisit semantics; re-presentation is a runtime property of the hub kind (no backward jump emitted).

addr.description: the record's resolved address (§4.2), unique within the artifact; jump/converge/target/body fields point at these.

cmdJump.description: Unconditional control-flow jump. Carries no stamp.

addr.description: the record's resolved address (§4.2), unique within the artifact; jump/converge/target/body fields point at these.

reason.description: free-form author string the host MAY surface (e.g. "completed"); Lute assigns it no meaning.

cmdEnd.description: dsl 0.8.0 §3: terminate the walk at this record. Equivalent to falling off the end of `commands`, except `reason` is carried. NEW in IR 0.8.0 — an engine implementing only 0.7 MUST refuse the artifact (unknown `kind` is a hard error).

addr.description: the record's resolved address (§4.2), unique within the artifact; jump/converge/target/body fields point at these.

at.description: the barrier time (authored duration, else max resolved clip end).

cmdBarrier.description: A timeline join point (§11.4). Carries no stamp.

addr.description: the record's resolved address (§4.2), unique within the artifact; jump/converge/target/body fields point at these.

rewards.description: dsl 0.16.0 §2/§3 declarative rewards — direct-child `<reward/>` entries of this quest in declaration order. Quest grants fire at fresh `complete`/`failed` transitions (spec §3 D-D). A `<reward on="failed"/>` entry fires ONLY on `failed` (authored fail OR §2.3 downward cascade); a default (no `on=`) entry fires ONLY on `complete`. Runs BEFORE the corresponding `questComplete`/`questFailed` handler bodies. Omitted when the quest authors no rewards (byte-identical to 0.15.1 for pre-rewards artifacts).

cmdQuest.description: <quest> declaration head (dsl 0.2.0 §6.3). A declaration head: objective completion bodies and <on> arms follow as their own addressed records.

addr.description: the record's resolved address (§4.2), unique within the artifact; jump/converge/target/body fields point at these.

body.description: addr of the action body segment.

cmdOn.description: <on> event-condition-action record (dsl 0.2.0 §4, §6.6): an independent event rule.

addr.description: the record's resolved address (§4.2), unique within the artifact; jump/converge/target/body fields point at these.

fields.description: resolved directive attrs, typed via the manifest AttrDecls.

effects.description: resolved plugin state-write bindings (IR A12); absent when the directive declares none.

command.description: One command record (§4.4), internally tagged on `kind`. An engine MUST error on an unknown `kind` (version-negotiation policy, top-level description); it MUST ignore unknown FIELDS within a known record.

artifactMeta.description: Kind-polymorphic envelope meta (untagged): SceneMeta when kind==scene, QuestMeta when kind==quest. The top-level allOf pins which by `kind`.

shot.description: 1-based document position of the shot (dsl 0.6.0 §3.2); matches the `addr` shot segment.

shotEntry.description: dsl 0.8.0 §6: one authored shot heading. Purely descriptive — control flow never references it.
